thread:
Alex: Quick poll — should we name the new office fern `release-candidate` or `hotfix`? :seedling:
Riley: `hotfix` feels honest. 99% chance someone forgets to water it and we ship a patch. :sweat_smile: 
Jamie: Oof. Can we at least tag it? `fern@main`? :plant: 
Sam: Imagine running `apply-plant.yaml` and getting a merge conflict.
Alex: Speaking of YAML, I found this in a config snippet in the kitchen:```yaml
plant: 
  name: release-candidate
  version: 1.0
  care: "water weekly"
```
Riley: `version: 1.0` — amateur. Needs at least semver. `1.0.0-olive` is the vibe.
Jamie: Please not another prerelease. Last time we had `v2.0-beta` on the whiteboard and it caused seven design debates.
Sam: DevBot, what's the recommended versioning strategy for potted plants? :robot_face:
DevBot: @Sam rule #1: Always use patch releases for watering. `1.0.1` for extra hydration. :thumbsup:
Alex: Also proposing labels: `needs-sun`, `low-maintenance`, `blames-ci`.
Riley: Add `blames-ci` as a tag and I will die laughing every time someone asks why the fern looks sad.
Jamie: Alternate idea: version the plant by compiler error messages it inspired. Example: `1.0.0-unexpected-token-in-pot`
Sam: I approve. We can keep a CHANGELOG.md on the fridge.
Alex: Vote time — react with :one: for `release-candidate`, :two: for `hotfix`, :three: for `fern@main`
Riley: Also, unrelated, whoever committed `tabs: true` to `.editorconfig` yesterday, you're on plant watering duties for a week. :joy: 
Jamie: Wait that was you, @Riley. :eyes:
Riley: Deny everything. :sunglasses: 
Sam: Closing poll at EOD — may the best version win. :trophy:
